results.name: Clio Manage Client Reports
results.title: Clio Manage Client Reports
results.body:
Reports in Clio Manage are designed to help your law firm track deliverables and get insights into all aspects of how the firm is performing. Client reports provide a comprehensive overview of client balances, bank account and matter transaction history, non-billable and billable work in progress, and trust account balances. On matters with multiple clients, most reports apply to the default client only. The Matter balance summary, Trust management, Invoice payments, Client Ledger, and Trust Listing reports support multiple clients on a matter.

See below for a summary of each client report in Clio Manage and what type of information the report offers.

Note: Every report in Clio is unique in the criteria it uses to calculate financial data. This means that comparing reports is not recommended. Additionally, not all reports are available for all Clio subscription plans. Learn more about reports available on your subscription plan and upgrading your plan here.

Client activity report

The client activity report is designed to give firms a detailed breakdown of billed and unbilled time and expense activities across matters. This report does not include non-billable time. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Date

This column shows the date that the activity was recorded. Multiple activities with the same date will appear in random order.

Activity type

This column shows whether the recorded activity is a time entry or expense entry.

Status

This column shows whether the activities are billed or unbilled. Activities are divided by billed and unbilled status, with billed activities appearing first with their subtotal, followed by unbilled activities.

User

This column lists the firm user who created the activity entry.

Activity category

This column shows the activity category recorded when the activity was created. If no activity category was selected, this column will be blank.

Description

This column shows the description entered when the activity entry was created.

Quantity

This column shows the total number of hours or expenses for the listed activity.

Price

This column shows the selected rate of the listed activities.

Total

This total summarizes the total cost of the time and expense entries. This value may be different from the value under the Price column depending on the Quantity. For example, if the Quantity for an activity is listed as 0.50, the Price is $500, then the Total would be $250.

Billed total

This total is the summarized total cost of billed time and expense entries for the matter.

Matter total

This total is the summarized total cost of billed time and expense entries for each of a client's matters.

Billed total

This total is the summarized total cost of billed time and expense entries for all of a client's matters.

 

Client ledger report

The client ledger report is designed to give firms a detailed view of client trust and operating transactions. This report also shows payments, refunds, transfers, and balances. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Date

This column shows the date that the transaction occurred in the account. Transactions include deposits, withdrawals, and transfers. Multiple transactions that occur on the same day will appear in random order.

Source/Destination

This column shows the payment type and is gathered from the Source/Destination field from when you are recording a new transaction.

Reference

This column shows data entered in the Reference field from when you recorded a new transaction.

Matter

This column shows the matter that is linked to the transaction.

Description

This column shows the information entered in the Description field from when you recorded a new transaction.

Funds out

This column lists withdrawals or payments from the account, including bank charges.

Funds in

This column lists payments deposited into the account, including interest earned.

Balance

This column shows the amount of money left in the account after each listed transaction.

Closing balance

This lists the closing balance of the Funds out, Funds in, and Balance.

Client total

This lists the total balance of the Funds out, Funds in, and Balance for all of the client's matters. If you have transactions across multiple operating and trust accounts, you may see different balances.

Balance summary

This section will appear at the bottom of the report if you selected the option for Display bank account summary before running the report. This section shows the current balance of your accounts. If you sort results by a specific date range, this section will show an opening balance that summarizes the transactions prior to the selected date range and a closing balance that summarizes the account balance at the end of the date range.

 

 

Trust ledger report

The trust ledger report is designed to give firms a detailed breakdown of client and matter transactions and balances across all trust accounts. The report includes payments, refunds, transfers, and balances. You can use this report to submit to regulators. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Date

This column shows the date that the transaction occurred in the account. Transactions include deposits, withdrawals, and transfers. Multiple transactions that occur on the same day will appear in random order.

Source/Destination

This column shows the payment type and is gathered from the Source/Destination field from when you are recording a new transaction. If you selected the option to Include opening balance before running the report, this section will first show the opening balance of each trust account, which is helpful if you choose to run the report in a specific date range.

Payer/Payee

This column shows information about the person making or receiving a payment. This information is useful when the payer or payee is not the client themselves.

Reference

This column shows data entered in the Reference field from when you recorded a new transaction.

Matter

This column shows the matter that is linked to the transaction.

Description

This column shows the information entered in the Description field from when you recorded a new transaction.

Funds out

This column lists withdrawals or payments from the account, including bank charges.

Funds in

This column lists payments deposited into the account, including interest earned.

Balance

This column shows the amount of money left in the account after each listed transaction.

Closing balance

This lists the closing balance of the Funds out, Funds in, and Balance.

Client total

This lists the total balance of the Funds out, Funds in, and Balance for all of the client's matters. If you have transactions across multiple operating and trust accounts, you may see different balances.

Balance summary

This section will appear at the bottom of the report if you selected the option for Display bank account summary before running the report. This section shows the current balance of your accounts. If you sort results by a specific date range, this section will show an opening balance that summarizes the transactions prior to the selected date range and a closing balance that summarizes the account balance at the end of the date range.

 

 

Trust interest calculation report

The trust interest calculation report is designed to calculate interest earned on deposited client matter trust funds across all trust accounts. You can use this report to calculate interest for trust funds based on rate, compounding period, and date range for a specific client or matter. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Date

This column shows the date that the transaction occurred in the account. Transactions include deposits, withdrawals, and transfers. Multiple transactions that occur on the same day will appear in random order.

Funds out

This column lists withdrawals or payments from the IOLTA account, including bank charges.

Funds in

This column lists trust funds deposited into the IOLTA account, including interest earned.

Balance

This column shows the amount of money remaining after each listed transaction.

Rate

This column lists the selected interest rate for each deposit.

Balance start date

The start date of the interest period as per the date range you selected to generate the report.

Balance end date

The end date of the interest period as per the date range you selected to generate the report.

Days held

This column shows the total number of days of the interest period you selected to generate the report.

Interest

This column shows the amount of interest accrued based on the balance for the selected period.

A summary of the Closing balance, Total interest, and Closing balance with interest is also provided for each calculation in the report.

If you generate this report in Clio, i.e., you generate a Web report, you have the option to post the calculated interest directly to the client funds you hold. Next to the Total interest amount calculated for the client funds held in a client funds account (per matter and client), click Apply Interest. You can change the transaction date and description for the transaction, then click Record transaction to create this ledger entry in the client funds account. The Source/Destination field for the entry will be “Trust Interest Calculation Report”.

Once you apply interest to the client funds, your subsequent Client funds interest reports will show the last five transactions where you applied interest to the account.

 

Trust management report

The trust management report is designed to give firms an overview of unbilled time and expense activities, trust account balances, and minimum trust thresholds. You can use this report to compare billable work against trust fund holdings. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Client

This column lists the name of each client

Matter

This column lists the matters for each client.

Unbilled amount

This column shows the amount of unbilled time and expense entries for each matter.

Amount in trust

This column shows the amount of funds currently in trust for the client or matter.

Minimum threshold

This column lists the minimum threshold set for matter trust funds. This amount can be changed by editing the matter and changing the number for Trust balance notification under Billing preference.

Amount below minimum

This column shows the amount that a trust balance has fallen below the minimum threshold set for the matter.

 

 

Trust listing report

The trust listing report is designed to give firms a quick summary of client trust fund balances across all client accounts. This report includes an opening and closing balance summary. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Account name

This column shows the name of the trust account.

Last activity date

This column shows the most recent transaction in the client's trust account.

Client balance

This column shows the current amount in trust for the client. This balance may be different from the amount shown in the matter's Dashboard if you generate the report for a specific date range. This means that if a client had trust funds in the account before that selected date range and payments were made during the date range, the report will only pull in transactions, which will result in a negative balance.

Unlinked

This section will appear at the bottom of the report if you selected the option for Include balances not associated with a client before running the report. It shows trust funds that are not linked to a specific client.

Balance summary

This section will appear at the bottom of the report if you selected the option for Display bank account summary before running the report. This section shows the current balance of your accounts. If you sort results by a specific date range, this section will show an opening balance that summarizes the transactions prior to the selected date range and a closing balance that summarizes the account balance at the end of the date range.

 

 

Work in progress report

The work in progress report is designed to give firms a detailed view of unbilled time and expense activities for matters. This report only shows activities on bills in draft, bills pending approval, and activities not on any bills. It will not show activities on any approved or paid bills. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Date

This column shows the date that the activity was recorded. Multiple activities with the same date will appear in random order.

User

This column lists the firm user assigned on the activity entry.

Description

This column shows the activity category selected when the activity was created. If no activity category was selected, this column will be blank.

Note

This column shows the description entered when the activity entry was created.

Quantity

This column shows the total number of hours or expenses.

Price

This column shows the selected rate of the listed activities.

Total

This total summarizes the total cost of the time and expense entries. This value may be different from the value under the Price column depending on the Quantity. For example, if the Quantity for an activity is listed as 0.50, the Price is $500, then the Total would be $250

Matter total

This total is the summarized total cost of unbilled time and expense entries for each of the client's matters.

Client total

This total is the summarized total cost of unbilled time and expense entries for all of the client's matters.

 

Bank account activity report

The bank account activity report is designed to give firms a detailed view of funds in and funds out across all firm bank accounts. This report also includes the account balance. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Date

This column shows the date that the transaction occurred in the account. Transactions include deposits, withdrawals, and transfers. Multiple transactions that occur on the same day will appear in random order.

Source/Destination

This column shows the payment type and is gathered from the Source/Destination field from when you are recording a new transaction. If you selected the option to Include opening balance before running the report, this section will first show the opening balance of each trust account, which is helpful if you choose to run the report in a specific date range.

Client

This column lists the client associated with the transaction.

Matter

This column shows the matter that is linked to the transaction.

Description

This column shows the information entered into the Description field when a payment was recorded.

Funds out

This column lists withdrawals or payments from the account, including bank charges.

Funds in

This column lists payments deposited into the account, including interest earned.

Balance

This column shows the amount of money left in the account after each listed transaction.

Closing balance

This lists the closing balance of the Funds out, Funds in, and Balance.

Balance summary

This section will appear at the bottom of the report if you selected the option for Display bank account summary before running the report. This section shows the current balance of your accounts. If you sort results by a specific date range, this section will show an opening balance that summarizes the transactions prior to the selected date range and a closing balance that summarizes the account balance at the end of the date range.

Next up

Learn more about generating reports, creating reports presets, and viewing a history of generated reports: Clio Manage Reports, Presets, and History.

results.name: Clio Manage Revenue Reports
results.title: Clio Manage Revenue Reports
results.body:
Reports in Clio Manage are designed to help your law firm track deliverables and get insights into all aspects of how the firm is performing. Revenue reports provide a comprehensive overview of your firm's financial performance by showing total collected activities and taxes, amounts generated by each originating attorney, and amounts each firm user has billed and collected for each matter. In each section below, a summary of a particular revenue report in Clio Manage is provided, along with details of the information the report offers.

Note: Every report in Clio is unique in the criteria it uses to calculate financial data. This means that comparing different types of reports is not recommended. Not all reports are available for all Clio subscription plans. Learn more about reports available on your subscription plan and upgrading your plan here.
Tip: For instructions about generating reports, creating reports presets (i.e., saving the filters used to generate a report), scheduling automated report generation, and viewing a history of generated reports, refer to Generate Reports, Presets, and History.

Revenue report

The revenue report is designed to give firms a detailed overview of unbilled, billed, and collected time and expense activities. This report also includes taxes, credit notes, discounted time, and discounted expenses by matter. You can use this report to help quantify key performance metrics on a per user, per client, and per matter basis.

Note: By default, partial payments and credit notes applied to invoices are allocated proportionally across all line items. If you change this setting to allocate partial payments and credit notes in a different way, the following columns will be calculated depending on the selected allocation method: Collected time, Collected expense, Collected tax 1, and Collected tax 2. Learn more about the reports allocation setting here.

When generated, the Web and PDF versions of the report includes the following columns:

Matter

This column lists the matter identifier. 

Location

This column shows the value entered in the Location field for a matter.  

Unbilled time

This column shows the monetary value of unbilled time entries for the matter. Unbilled time entries are time entries that are not generated on any approved bills, including time entries that are not on a bill and time entries that are on bills in draft or bills pending approval.

Unbilled hours

This column shows unbilled time entry hours for the matter. Unbilled time entries are those that do not yet appear on any approved bills, i.e., time entries that are either not on a bill or on a bill in a draft state or pending approval.

Unbilled expense

This column shows the monetary value of unbilled expense entries for the matter. Unbilled expense entries are expenses that are not generated on any approved bills, including expenses that are not on a bill and expenses that are on bills in draft or bills pending approval.

Billed time

This column shows the monetary value of billed time entries for the matter. Billed time entries are time entries on approved bills.

Billed hours

This column shows billed time entry hours for the matter. Billed time entries are time entries on approved bills.

Billed expense

This column shows the dollar value of billed expense entries for the matter. Billed expense entries are expenses on approved bills.

Billed tax 1

This column shows the dollar value of your first tax on billed activities for the matter. Billed activities are billable time and expense entries on approved bills.

Billed tax 2

This column shows the dollar value of your second tax on billed activities for the matter. Billed activities are billable time and expense entries on approved bills.

Discounted time

This column shows the dollar value of billed time entries for the matter that had discounts applied to them. Billed time entries are time entries on approved bills.

Discounted expense

This column shows the dollar value of billed expense entries for the matter that had discounts applied to them. Billed expense entries are expenses on approved bills.

Credit notes

This column shows the dollar value of billed activities for the matter that had credit notes applied to them. Billed activities are time and expense entries on approved bills.

Collected time

This column shows the dollar value of billed time entries on generated bills that have been paid. If a partial payment was applied to a bill with time entries, the payment will be evenly applied across the Collected time, Collected expense, Collected tax, and Collected tax 2 columns. 

Collected expense

This column shows the dollar value of billed expense entries on generated bills that have been paid. If a partial payment was applied to a bill with expenses, the payment will be evenly applied across the Collected time, Collected expense, Collected tax 1, and Collected tax 2 columns.

Collected tax 1

This column shows the dollar value of your first tax on billed activities on generated bills that have been paid. If a partial payment was applied to a bill, the payment will be evenly applied across the Collected time, Collected expense, Collected tax 1, and Collected tax 2 columns.

Collected tax 2

This column shows the dollar value of your second tax on billed activities on generated bills that have been paid. If a partial payment was applied to a bill, the payment will be evenly applied across the Collected time, Collected expense, Collected tax 1, and Collected tax 2 columns.

Collected uncategorized

This column refers to collected money that is not attached to any matter or client.

Client total

This total refers to the total of each column for all of the client's matters. 

Summary information and totals are displayed at the bottom of the report.

No client/No practice area

This section will appear at the bottom of the report if you have revenue that is not attached to any client or practice area. The heading of the section (No Client vs No Practice Area) will depend on whether you grouped your results by client or practice area when you selected your options for generating the report.

Clio Scheduler payments

This section will appear at the bottom of the report and shows revenue for payments collected through Clio Scheduler appointments.

Total

The final line of the report provides the grand totals of all columns.

Reports in CSV and Excel format have the same columns as the Web and PDF reports along with some additional columns.

Client

Since the reports in CSV and Excel format are not grouped by client or practice area, this column shows the client name for the matter.

Practice Area

Since the reports in CSV and Excel format are not grouped by client or practice area, this column shows the practice area for the matter.

Matter Description

The description of the matter.

Responsible Attorney

The name of the Attorney assigned as responsible for the Matter.

Billed Interest

The monetary value of interest on overdue (approved) bills.

Collected Interest

The monetary value of interest collected on overdue bills.

It is useful to understand the details about which information is included in or excluded from the report depending on the date range selected when generating the report.

Expense and time entries have more than one date associated with it. For example, an entry has a date of creation, i.e. the date the entry was recorded in Clio, and the date that a bill was issued for the entry. These entries are included or excluded based on the following rules:

  • Unbilled information will be included if the date the entry was created falls within the date range selected when generating the report.
  • Billed information will be included if the bill issue date for that entry falls within the date range selected when generating the report.
  • Collected amounts and information will be included if the payment date falls within the date range selected when generating the report.

Credit notes appear on the report if the date the credit note was created falls within the date range selected when generating the report.

Originating attorney revenue report

The originating attorney revenue report is designed to help firms visualize and quantify how much revenue each attorney in the firm has brought in. This report includes taxes, interest, fees, and collected time and expense activities.

Note: This report only reflects the Originating Lawyer set in a matter's Matter Details section. It does not reflect the role allocations, percentages, or additional users set in the firm's fee allocation settings or fee allocation settings applied to the matter. To report on fee allocation that includes those, use the Fee allocation dataset in Custom Reports.

Note: By default, partial payments and credit notes applied to invoices are allocated proportionally across all line items. If you change this setting to allocate partial payments and credit notes in a different way, the following columns will be calculated depending on the selected allocation method: Collected time, Collected expense, Collected tax, and Collected tax 2. Learn more about the reports allocation setting here.

When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Attorney

This column lists the firm user who is designated as the originating attorney on a matter.

Collected time

This column shows the total value of the originating attorney's time entries on bills that have been paid. 

Collected expense

This column shows the total value of the originating attorney's expense entries on bills that have been paid. 

Collected interest

This column shows the total value of the interest on bills that have been paid for the originating attorney on the matter. 

Collected tax

This column shows the total value of the first tax on bills that have been paid for the originating attorney on the matter. 

Collected secondary tax

This column shows the total value of the second tax on bills that have been paid for the originating attorney on the matter. 

Grand total

This total summarizes the total collected amounts for each column for this originating attorney.

 

Fee allocation report

The fee allocation report is designed to give firms a detailed view of time and expenses each firm user has billed and collected for each matter. This report also includes accounts receivables and credit notes. You can use this report to determine your firm’s bonus payout to attorneys.

Note: This report only reflects the Originating Lawyer set in a matter's Matter Details section. It does not reflect the role allocations, percentages, or additional users set in the firm's fee allocation settings or fee allocation settings applied to the matter. To report on fee allocation that includes those, use the Fee allocation dataset in Custom Reports or use the Clio-built Fee allocation report in the Clio tab of Custom Report.

Note: By default, partial payments and credit notes applied to invoices are allocated proportionally across all line items. If you change this setting to allocate partial payments and credit notes in a different way, the columns listed below will be calculated depending on the selected allocation method. Learn more about the reports allocation setting here.

  • Billed time collected
  • Billing time outstanding
  • Expense amount collected (CSV only)
  • Expense amount outstanding (CSV only)
  • Primary tax collected (CSV only)
  • Primary tax outstanding (CSV only)
  • Secondary tax collected (CSV only)
  • Secondary tax outstanding (CSV only)

When generated, this report includes the following categories:

User

This column lists the firm user who created the activity entry. In the Web report, the report is organized into user sections.

Matter

This column lists the matter for which a firm user has billed and collected time and/or expenses. In the Web report, you can click on the matter to navigate to it. Use your browser’s back button to return to the report from the matter.

Client

This column lists the client for each matter. In the Web report, you can click on the client name to navigate to their details. Use your browser’s back button to return to the report from the contact.

Invoice

This column lists the bill invoice number for the matter. In the Web report, you can click on the invoice number to view invoice details. Use your browser’s back button to return to the report from the invoice.

Practice area

This column shows the practice area for the matter. If a practice area was not selected, this column will be blank.

Responsible attorney

This column shows the responsible attorney assigned to the matter.

Originating attorney

This column shows the originating attorney assigned to the matter.

Billed hours

This column shows the total hours that a firm user spent on the activities on a bill that is approved but unpaid or a bill that has been paid. This information is pulled directly from the listed bill invoice. Credit notes and write-offs will not affect the number of billed hours but discounts will affect the number of billed hours.

Billed time

This column shows the dollar value of the time entries a specific firm user generated on a bill that is approved but unpaid or a bill that has been paid. This information is pulled directly from the listed bill invoice. Credit notes and write-offs will not affect billed time but discounts will affect billed time.

Billed time allocation

This column refers to the percentage of billed time on a bill that a user is responsible for. If multiple firm users have time entries on a single bill, this column will show the percentage of time that each user is responsible for.

Collected time

This columns shows the dollar value of the time entries on bills that have been paid.

Outstanding time

This column shows the dollar value of the time entries on bills that are approved but have not been paid.

Billed expense

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It shows the dollar value of the expenses a specific firm user generated on a bill that is approved but unpaid or a bill that has been paid.

Expense allocation

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It shows the percentage of billed expenses on a bill that a user is responsible for. If multiple firm users have expense entries on a single bill, this column will show the percentage of expenses that each user is responsible for.

Collected expense

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It shows the dollar value of the expense entries on bills that have been paid.

Outstanding expense

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It shows the dollar value of the expense entries on bills that are approved but have not been paid.

Total collected

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It is the total amount of payments applied to specific bills.

Total outstanding

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It is the total amount of unpaid time and expenses on specific bills.

Interest collected

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It shows the total dollar value of the interest on bills that have been paid.

Interest outstanding

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It shows the total dollar value of the interest on bills that are approved but have not been paid.

Collected tax 1

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It shows the total dollar value of the primary tax on bills that have been paid.

Outstanding tax 1

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It shows the total dollar value of the primary tax on bills that are approved but have not been paid.

Collected tax 2

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It shows the total dollar value of the secondary tax on bills that have been paid.

Outstanding tax 2

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It shows the total dollar value of the secondary tax on bills that are approved but have not been paid.

Collected time allocated to responsible attorney

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It shows the total dollar value of collected time to allocate to the responsible attorney.

Collected time allocated to originating attorney

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It shows the total dollar value of collected time to allocate to the originating attorney.

Matter billing method

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It shows the billing method selected on the matter, with options for contingency, flat fee, or hourly.

Non-billable time amount

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It shows the dollar value of the non-billable time entries a specific firm user generated for that matter.

Non-billable time allocation

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. This column refers to the percentage of non-billable time on a matter that a firm user is responsible for.

  • Billed information will be included if the bill issue date for that entry falls within the date range selected when generating the report.

results.title: Email Marketing in Clio Grow
results.body:
With Clio Grow, you can build and send high-quality email campaigns to engage with leads and clients. Once enabled, email marketing is accessible to all users in your firm who have access to Clio Grow. You can use email marketing campaigns to curate emails that help your firm stay top of mind, convert leads to clients, and secure repeat business. The reporting features for email marketing can also help you understand how well your campaign performed, how recipients interact with your campaigns, and how much revenue you drive from email campaigns.

Tip: Leverage information about your contacts—such as contact tags and contact types—to send emails that are relevant to them. If you also use Clio Manage, ensure that you enable shared contacts between Clio Manage and Clio Grow to receive help with premade campaigns.

 

Create an email marketing campaign

The email marketing campaign feature in Clio Grow guides you through every step of creating effective email campaigns. Depending on the nature of the campaign, you may need to return to the draft campaign more than once to modify and refine it. Clio Grow makes this easy by autosaving your campaign as you work. If you are working with other firm users on an email campaign, to minimize the risk of accidentally overwriting another user's work in the campaign builder, draft your email copy and brainstorm subject lines outside of the Clio Grow campaign builder.

Step 1: Create a new campaign
  1. In Clio Grow, click the main Marketing tab.
  2. Click Create campaign.

  3. Select from one of the existing campaign objectives or click Create a custom campaign.

    Tip: If you use Clio Manage in addition to Clio Grow, you can also explore the premade campaigns available to you. For each campaign, a relevant list of recipients and content has already been started for you. To get the most out of premade campaigns, make sure that you opt in to shared contacts.
Step 2: Define the campaign

  1. Optional: Click Edit name to update the campaign name.

    Note: The campaign name is for internal use and will not appear on any sent campaign emails. It is used as the marketing source label that is added to a matter. In turn, this marketing source can then be used to track metrics and matter revenue attributed to the campaign. Learn more about marketing sources here.
  2. Describe the campaign objective.
    • If you are using one of the ready-to-use campaigns, you will not be able to change the objective.
Step 3: Curate a list of recipients

You can curate your list of recipients to suit your needs by using appropriate filters, along with contact tags, contact types, and other recipient characteristics. Clio also helps you to protect your sender's reputation by automatically removing recipients who are more likely to report your emails as spam. Clio may remove recipients to whom previous emails bounced or recipients that your firm did not formally engage with, for example, those with Did not Hire statuses. Note that the latter scenario would not apply to certain campaign objectives that aim to revive lost opportunities. In addition, those who have unsubscribed from your emails on a previous campaign will also be removed from your list of recipients.

  1. Click the Recipients section to expand it.
  2. Click Add filters for the Include or Exclude options based on how you want to filter recipients based on their characteristics.
    1. For available filter options and their meanings, refer to Understand filter options to select your recipients.
  3. Select from the available options in the drop-down, then set the value(s) to filter upon.
    • The number of contacts that meet the criteria of your filters will update as you add and remove filters.
  4. Optional: Repeat the steps above to add additional filters. To remove a filter or value, click the X next to it.

  5. Optional: To manually remove a contact from the list of recipients, click View to see the list of your contacts, then click Remove in the row of the individual you want to remove.

    Note: In your Recipients list you can toggle between the Included and Removed options to see the individuals in their respective lists. You can also continue to Remove or Include previously removed individuals from their respective lists. If you apply additional filters or remove filters with your Recipients list open, click Refresh to apply the filter changes to the list of contacts. Some recipients may appear in your Removed
  6. When you are satisfied with your final list of contacts, click Next.
Important: If the number of contacts in your segment exceeds 5,000, you will be notified that only the newest 5,000 contacts will be included.

Ensure that your contacts’ email addresses are up to date to minimize the risk of email bouncing, which can occur when the email address is no longer valid or the inbox is full due to inactivity. Higher bounce rates may negatively impact your sender reputation and reduce the effectiveness of your campaign due to a lower delivery rate. You can refer to View campaign metrics to learn how to monitor relevant campaign metrics in the email marketing recipient report. Also, make sure that the content you plan to create is relevant to your list of contacts. Recipients may not find an email relevant if it is too broad, thereby increasing the risk of it being labeled as spam.

Step 4: Create your content
Tip: If you are unsure where to start, consider using the AI email feature for inspiration. To learn more, see Use AI to create your email copy.

  1. Add an email subject line.

    Tip: A short and meaningful subject line with appropriate capitalization and punctuation are less likely to be marked as spam, as is a subject line that avoids misleading or sensationalized statements. A curated subject line minimizes the risk of your email being marked as spam, thereby maintaining your sender reputation and ensuring a high deliverability rate.
  2. Create the body of the email. Provide information about how the email should address the contact.

    • Greeting format: Use the Contact name options dropdown to select how the recipient will be addressed. When you select an option, the text in brackets in the Greeting format represents your selection and serves as a placeholder for the recipient's details. You can edit text outside of the brackets. As an example, “Happy holidays, [First Name]!” would display as “Happy holidays, Gabriela!”

      Note: To comply with anti-spam laws, your firm’s name and address in Clio Grow will automatically be added to emails, along with the option for the recipient to unsubscribe from emails.
  3. When the subject line and content are ready, click Next.
Note: Campaigns autosave as you work. Find your draft campaigns in the Email campaigns table.
Step 5: Send the campaign

  1. Optional, but recommended: Click Send test email > Send test email to preview what your email will look like to recipients and to review the subject line, greeting, email body, sign off, and the firm signature (firm name and address) for any issues or errors.

    Note: Check your spam folder if you do not see the test email in your inbox.

  2. Once you are satisfied with the email, click Send email > Send email.

    Important: This action cannot be undone. Only send the email when you are certain all aspects of the campaign have been reviewed.

Your email campaign will be sent to recipients in sequential batches over a short period.

 

Edit or delete in-progress campaigns

Campaigns that have not yet been sent can be edited and/or deleted.

Edit Delete
Important: When editing an existing email campaign that other Clio Grow users are also contributing to, ensure you communicate with those collaborators. Clio Grow’s email campaign builder autosaves as you work to make sure no changes are lost, but this may cause work to be overwritten if two or more users are simultaneously working on the same campaign.
  1. In Clio Grow, go to the main Marketing tab.
  2. Click the name of the relevant campaign (with a Draft status), or click Actions > Edit.
  1. In Clio Grow, go to the main Marketing tab.
  2. For the the relevant campaign (with a Draft status) click Actions > Delete.
  3. Click Delete campaign to confirm the action.
Important: Deleted campaigns cannot be recovered.

 

Understand filter options to select your recipients

The following filter options are available to create a segment.

Contact tag is: Contact tags in Clio Grow allow you to add any identifier to your contacts. Learn more about creating Grow tags and adding them to contacts.

Contact type is: Contact types in Clio Grow allow you to distinguish between contacts who are leads, clients, or those who did not retain your services. Learn more about contact types.

Matter type is: Matter type in Clio Grow provides information about the practice area of the matter. Learn more about matter types in Clio Grow and how to create and manage matter types.

Matter status is: Matter status in Clio Grow provides a measure of the stage a matter is in, from its creation to its conclusion. You may recognize these as the statuses in the Pipeline columns. Learn more about how to create and manage matter statuses in Clio Grow.

Form is pending since: When you send a form to a Clio Grow contact and before the contact fills and submits the form, it will be in a pending state. You can view all pending forms in Forms > Pending. This field allows you to filter contacts with pending forms based on the date the form was sent.

Document is pending since: When you send a document to a Clio Grow contact and before the contact fills and submits the form, it will be in a pending state. You can view all pending forms in Forms > Pending. This field allows you to filter contacts with pending forms based on the date the form was sent.

Practice area is: Practice area is information synced from Clio Manage. It provides information about the practice area of the matter. Learn more about matter types in Clio Manage and how to create and manage practice areas.

Matter close date is between: This field allows you to filter contacts based on the date a matter status was set to 'Close'.

 

Use AI to create your email copy

If you are not sure where to start with creating clear and engaging content that follows best practices for email marketing campaigns, you can use the AI feature to help you create the subject line, greeting, and body of the email (i.e., step 4 in Create an Email marketing campaign). Ensure that your recipients are added before using the AI feature, so that the suggested content is tailored to them.

Note: In some instances the AI feature may not be able to generate content that is relevant to or appropriate for the list of recipients. When this happens, try adjusting your list of recipients to generate different content.
  1. In the Content block, click Draft email.
  2. Optional: If you are not satisfied with the draft and would like the AI to try again, click the regenerate icon (next to Drafted by AI).
  3. When you are generally satisfied with the AI-generated draft, click Insert email.
    • This will populate the various fields in the Content blocks with the AI-generated text.
  4. Make any required adjustments to the Subject, Greeting format, Contact name options, and Body, then click Next.
  5. Proceed as you usually would with sending the email.

 

Manage campaigns

In the main Marketing tab, your Email campaigns table will show the status and key results of your campaigns. The table provides the following information about each campaign:

  • Name: The campaign name.
    • You can click on the campaign name of in-progress campaigns to continue editing the campaign, and on the campaign name of sent campaigns to review campaign performance.
  • Status: The status of the campaign
    • For one of the campaigns, you can see statuses of Draft, Sending…, Sent, or Failed.
    • For ongoing campaigns, like birthday email campaigns, you can see statuses of Active and Pause.
  • Date launched: The date and time the campaign was sent.
  • Recipients: The number of contacts to whom the email was sent.
  • Opens: The percentage of recipients who opened an email.
  • Clicks: The percentage of delivered emails that were opened by the recipient.
  • Actions: You’ll be able to take different actions and/or view additional information about each campaign depending on the Status of the campaign. Campaigns with Draft status can be edited or deleted, and campaigns with a Sent status can be viewed or reviewed for their metrics. Click Actions for the relevant email campaign to access these options.
    • Draft: A campaign in Draft status can be edited or deleted.
    • Sending: A campaign is currently in the Sending status. You will have to wait for the sending to complete before taking any action.
    • Sent: You can review a summary about any campaign with a Sent status, using the View campaign option in the Actions dropdown. Your campaign page will display the following information about your campaign performance. Primary subscribers and those with Admin permissions will also be able to view more details about each Sent campaign, using the View recipient report option in the Actions dropdown. Learn more about this report below.
    • Active: Ongoing email campaigns that are active will have an option to Pause. You can also view metrics using the View campaign and View recipient report options.
    • Pause: Ongoing email campaigns that are paused will have an option to Activate. You can also view metrics using the View campaign and View recipient report options.

 

Activate automated campaigns

Note: The automated campaigns feature is available to firms with Clio Grow AI.

To help your firm stay top of mind year-round, you can create and activate automated campaigns that send emails to clients when certain conditions are met. For example, a birthday campaign will send congratulatory birthday emails to your contacts with dates of birth on file. Once you activate an automated email campaign, you cannot delete or edit it in order to preserve data about any emails that were already sent as part of the campaign. If you want to change an automated campaign you can pause your existing campaign and create a new one.

Note: Automated sending is available for all Premade campaigns.
CreatePauseReactivate
  1. In Clio Grow, click the main Marketing tab.
  2. In the Premade campaigns section click View campaign for one of the suggested campaigns, or click Explore more for additional options.
  3. Click Create campaign.
  4. Optional: Edit the campaign.
    1. Edit the campaign name. Refer to step 2 in Create an Email marketing campaign for details.

    2. Edit the automation rules. Depending on the type of campaign, the trigger for the automation can be

      • the date that the matter was closed or
      • the contact's date of birth (for birthday campaigns).

      Set the amount of time to wait after the trigger condition is met before the email should be sent to a contact.

    3. Modify the recipient list as needed. Refer to step 3 in Create an Email marketing campaign for details.
    4. Edit the email content. Refer to step 4 in Create an Email marketing campaign for details.
  5. Once you have completed all details, click Activate campaign, then confirm this action by clicking Activate campaign again.

Once activated, birthday campaigns will send emails to recipients at 9:00 AM PDT on their birthday, and other automated campaigns will send emails to recipients at 9:00 AM PDT on the first business day after the trigger condition is met and the amount of time to wait has lapsed. To review the emails sent with automatic campaigns, view the Email marketing recipient report for the campaign.

You can also pause and reactivate automated email campaigns. To pause a campaign:

  1. In Clio Grow, click the main Marketing tab.
  2. For the (active) campaign you want to pause, click Actions > Pause campaign.
  3. In the modal, click Pause campaign again to confirm.

To reactivate a campaign:

  1. In Clio Grow, click the main Marketing tab.
  2. For the campaign you want to pause, click Actions > Activate campaign.
  3. In the modal, click Activate campaign again to confirm.

 

View campaign metrics

Primary subscribers and those with Admin permissions can view summary metrics and the email marketing recipient report for each sent campaign to glean insight into the email delivery and recipient engagement with the email campaign. The email marketing recipient report provides per-recipient information about the number of emails that were opened and unopened, how each recipient interacted with the email (e.g., clicking links in the email), which recipients unsubscribed, and per-recipient emails that bounced or failed to send.

View summary metrics

To view a summary of the email marketing campaign:

  1. In Clio Grow, go to the main Marketing tab.
  2. Click the name of the relevant (sent) campaign, or click Actions, then select View campaign.

This view provides a summary of the key metrics of the campaign. The summary provides information about the total number of email sent, the delivery rate, open rate, click rate, unsubscribe rate, and the rate at which the email was reported as spam. Values are prominently displayed as percentages with absolute counts provided as smaller text.

  • Total emails sent: The number of emails sent out in the campaign.
  • Delivery: This value indicates the percentage/number of sent messages that successfully reached the recipient’s inbox.
  • Opens: This value indicates the percentage/number of unique recipients who opened an email. If a recipient opens an email several times, this will only count as one open.
  • Clicks: This value is a measure of recipient interaction with your email campaign. A recipient that interacts with your email (e.g., by clicking a link in your campaign) is counted as a unique click. A recipient that has several interactions with the email will still be counted as one unique click.
  • Unsubscribes: This value indicates the percentage/number of recipients who unsubscribed.
  • Reported as spam: This value indicates the percentage/number of recipients who reported this email as spam.

 

View detailed metrics

You can also view more detailed metrics in the recipient report, which includes recipient-specific details for a particular campaign:

  1. In Clio Grow, go to the main Marketing tab.
  2. For the relevant (sent) campaign, click Actions, then select View recipient report.

This report includes information about each contact to whom the report was sent.

  • Contact: This column shows the name of the recipient. The table is sorted alphabetically by first name. You can click on a contact name to open a new tab with the contact’s details. Learn more about Clio Grow contacts here.
  • Email sent to: This column displays the primary email address associated with the contact.
  • Campaign source: This column shows the name of the campaign.
  • Delivery: This column shows if the email was Delivered or if it Bounced (i.e., it could not be delivered due to issues such as a full email inbox or an email address that does not exist).
  • Date sent: This columns shows the date that the email was sent.
  • Opened: This column shows if the email was opened by the recipient.
  • Clicked: This column shows if the recipient interacted with the email (e.g., by clicking on a link in the email).
  • Unsubscribed: This column shows if the recipient unsubscribed. If they did, the columns will display as Unsubscribed, Otherwise it will be empty (-).
  • Intake matters: The number of matters for the recipient that is in an intake state and where the matter’s most recent marketing source is the current email marketing campaign. Learn more about how marketing sources are assigned to matters.
  • Hired matters: The number of matters for the recipient that is in a hired state and where the matter’s most recent marketing source is the current email marketing campaign. Learn more about how marketing sources are assigned to matters.
  • Revenue: The revenue produced for this recipient as a result of the relevant email campaign.

 

Email campaigns as marketing sources

A set of rules determine if activities associated with a matter or revenue generated by a matter should be attributed to a particular email marketing campaign. If an email with a particular objective is opened by a recipient, and a particular event is logged in Clio Grow (e.g., a new matter is created for the recipient) within a set number of days of the email being opened, the email marketing campaign will be added to the matter as a marketing source. 

To view the email marketing sources for any matter:

  1. In Clio Grow, click the main Matters tab.
  2. In the Matter name column, click the relevant matter.

The Marketing section in the left information panel of the matter will display the first and most recent marketing sources associated with the matter, as well as the total number of marketing sources associated with the matter. Learn how to view the full list of marketing sources here.

The following information provides details about the unique cases that you may see and the rules that determine how email marketing campaigns are added to matters.

  • If you created a Hire prospective clients email campaign, generated revenue will be attributed to the email campaign if the following applies:
    • The recipient opened the email and their existing matter (with a status of Intake) was updated within 7 days of the email being opened.
  • If you created a Revive lost opportunities email campaign, generated revenue will be attributed to the email campaign if the following applies:
    • The recipient opened the email and their existing matter (with a status of Did not hire) was updated within 30 days of the email being opened.
  • If you created an Increase repeat business or Stay top of mind email campaign or you opted to Create a custom campaign, generated revenue will be attributed to the email campaign if the following applies:
    • The recipient opened the email and a new matter was created within 30 days of the email being opened.

Add email campaigns for attribution

The rules that determine how email marketing campaign labels are added as marketing sources to matters can provide an overview of how matter revenue can be attributed to various email campaigns. You can still manually add, edit, or delete email marketing campaigns associated with a matter.

 

View sent marketing emails by contact

An email sent to a contact as part of a marketing campaign will be logged in the contact’s communications, unless the email failed to send or bounced.

  1. Click Contacts.
  2. Click the name of the contact.

  3. Click Communications.

    Note: Emails sent via marketing campaign will appear in this tab and be labeled Marketing email.

 

Understand and manage consent

In Canada you must obtain consent before sending marketing emails. Clio Grow makes it easy to capture, track, and manage consent. You can capture consent to receive marketing emails directly from your clients by including a check box for them to check on your intake forms. Or, you can also select the consent check box on their behalf (after receiving your client's verbal consent) when you create a Quick Appointment or when you create a new contact and their matter via the Quick Intake form.

Important: Your firm remains responsible for capturing and managing consent in a way that complies with your region’s legal requirements.

Note: Capturing consent for email marketing is a new feature that affects the following Clio Grow intake methods:

  • Intake forms
  • Website form
  • Appointment links

A Subscribe to email marketing check box will be added to each of these intake methods where contacts can opt in to marketing emails from your firm. Make sure to review each of these intake methods if you do not want to include this field. You will still be required to adhere to capturing consent from your contacts if you want to send them marketing emails.

To carefully track the various scenarios of how consent is obtained, the following distinctions are used in Clio Grow. 

  • Explicit consent: Explicit consent refers to scenarios where the client actively opts into receiving marketing emails. Clients can opt verbally to a member of your firm in which case the firm member can log this information in Clio Grow when they create a Quick Appointment, create a new contact and their matter via the Quick Intake form, or edit a contact. Clients can also opt in themselves by checking the relevant check box on an intake form you send them. When explicit consent is given, the client is subscribed to email marketing and the method of consent (via firm member, intake form, appointment link, website form, or website chat) and the date and time is logged in the contact's details in Clio Grow.

  • Implicit consent: When a client enters a professional relationship with your firm, they can be said to have implicitly consented to receive marketing emails. Implied consent remains valid for two years after the business relationship concludes. 

    In Clio Grow, the business relationship starts—and implicit consent is assumed—when a contact's status is set to Hired. If no further activity occurs on the matter, this date is then also the date that the relationship "concludes". In this case where there is no further activity, the implicit consent will lapse two years after the contact's status changed to Hired. 

    However, if activity commences on the client's matter and the matter is synced to Clio Manage, the date that the business relationship concludes coincides with the date that you close the matter in Clio Manage.

    With implicit consent, the client is subscribed to email marketing, and you can view this information when you view their contact details in Clio Grow.

When either implicit or explicit consent applies, the contact is subscribed to email marketing. Your contact can also unsubscribe from email marketing by clicking Unsubscribe on a marketing email they received, or by asking a member at your firm to unsubscribe them.

Important: Your contact can also be "Not subscribed" for marketing emails. This differs from being "Unsubscribed" in that "Not subscribed means that the contact simply never indicated any preference to receiving or not receiving marketing emails.
